look_here_first: Look for a leafless flower stalk with a terminal umbel of funnel-shaped six-tepaled flowers. Look into the throat for the distinctive crown made by joined stamen filaments. Confirm basal linear leaves; do not use flower color alone.
taxonomy_notes: Androstephium caeruleum is an orthographic variant of coeruleum, not a second species. Historical names Milla coerulea and Brodiaea coerulea refer to the same concept. County-native certification pending.

morphology_keys.habit: Small spring perennial from corm; glabrous leafless scape 10–20(–35) cm.
morphology_keys.leaves: Several narrow basal leaves 10–30(–35) cm long and 1.5–3 mm wide.
morphology_keys.flower_attachment: Terminal umbel of 2–6(–9) stalked flowers, pedicels about 1–2(–2.5) cm.
morphology_keys.flowers: Six partly united tepals form a funnel; perianth 1.5–2.5(–3) cm. Six stamen filaments form an inner crown; anthers 2–4 mm.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Three-angled capsules 1–1.5 cm; flat black seeds 7–9 mm.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Check the joined tepal funnel and filament-built central crown against false garlic and Allium; A. breviflorum is a separate western species.
